Graph, node detail and worker inputs already iterated the given workers; verified, no other hardcoded lane names remained. Tests: tests/project-workflows/fixtures.ts (new lanes-flow workflow with run-three-lanes [ui, adapter, docs] and run-one-lane [docs only, ui/adapter excluded] at contract/export 1.3.0 with selected_workers, excluded_workers, required_check_kinds, a docs finding, a 'multiple' finding and a legacy 'both' finding; existing two-lane raw sections unchanged; projections at contract 1.3.0 with role-derived kinds for 1.2.0 exports), seed.ts (per-lane packets and receipts; 1.3.0 exports with plan.workers/excluded_workers and values.lanes/values.packets), mock.ts (runs scoped per workflow), support.ts (runUrl takes a workflow), lanes.spec.ts (new: [scenario:viewer-three-lanes], [scenario:legacy-run] with screenshot:<id> attachments). In this worktree alone (contract still 1.2.0): npm run build fails with TS2339 on selected_workers/excluded_workers/required_check_kinds and the browser suite fails at fixture load (contract_version 1.3.0 rejected by the 1.2.0 schema); both are the expected dependency on the adapter lane's contract change and pass once it is present. No candidate-phase run was executed in this worktree alone.
open_assumptions: The projects contract 1.3.0 keeps inputs.workers as an ordered array (node_id any lane id) with required_check_kinds, plus selected_workers and excluded_workers on inputs; finding worker and requirement_found_in are strings; contract_version is the literal '1.3.0' for review and inputs payloads. This matches the adapter worktree's contracts/projects/v1.ts as of this handoff.

1.3.0 exports keep per-lane state under values.lanes[<id>] and values.packets[<id>] (PRD section 4); the adapter's server reads both this and the flat legacy keys, so the seeds use the nested shape only.

A 1.2.0 export projects to contract 1.3.0 with selected_workers = every listed lane, excluded_workers = [] and required_check_kinds derived from the role (frontend: build, browser; backend: unit), as verification.py did before policy 1.2.0.

The new runs live in a separate registered workflow (lanes-flow) in the same project so the feature-flow run list and the existing scenarios' counts are untouched; the one-lane run is a --workers docs subset of the three-lane policy.

The lane's own worker-phase verification (build and browser checks on this worktree in isolation) cannot pass until the adapter's contract change is present; the candidate phase combining both lanes is where these checks are expected to pass.

adapter.summary: Implemented PRD_WORKER_LANES slice A on the controller, contracts and server adapter. Contracts: verification.schema.json 1.2.0 (unbounded workers, lane-id pattern with reserved names, free role, required_check_kinds, failure_drill.node_id any lane; 1.0.0/1.1.0 still accepted), new feature.schema.json (2.0.0), reviewCompletion.schema.json 1.1.0 (worker is a lane id, multiple or none; both refused), updated example, README and contract.test.ts; contracts/projects 1.3.0 (role string, required_check_kinds, selected_workers, excluded_workers, finding worker as lane-id string, requirement_found_in as lane ids), examples, tests, README, regenerated JSON schemas. workflow/: NODES deleted; plan-driven prepare (declared lanes, pinned workers/excluded_workers/failure_drill), ClaudeSessions, build_pipeline over plan.workers with lanes/packets state, ownership against excluded lanes, ordered candidate, --task/--handoff <id>=<path>, --workers at launch and prepare, --node validated against the run, plan-driven panes and observer, reviewer vocabulary and print-mode schema from the plan with lane validation of findings, export 1.3.0 with a dynamic definition (stored definitions kept on re-export, legacy checkpoint lane evidence carried under values.lanes/packets), computed report positions; feature 2.0.0 with 1.0.0 translation plus deprecation line; graph.py, demo.py, live.py, test_graph.py deleted and SessionState moved to sessions.py. server/projects.ts accepts exports 1.0.0-1.3.0, derives lanes from inputs.workers with the fixed pair as the no-inputs fallback, maps launch_/verify_/candidate_ nodes by naming, accepts legacy both; projects.test.ts gains three-lane and one-lane exports. features/project-workflows migrated to feature.json 2.0.0 and policy.json 1.2.0 (ui: build, browser; adapter: unit). RUNBOOK, CHEATSHEET, feature README, contracts/workflow README and the secondary workflow docs updated. New workflow/test_lanes.py covers three-lane-run, one-lane-run, subset-pinned, excluded-ownership, unknown-worker, required-kinds, reserved-id, retry-any-lane, drill-skipped, finding-lane, legacy-feature, the export half of legacy-run and an offline pane-order check. Checks executed in this worktree on the final tree: .venv python -m unittest discover -s workflow -t . (136 tests OK, 276s), npm run test:contracts (17 pass), npm run test:unit (130 pass), npm run build (passed, pre-existing chunk-size warning), npm run lint (passed), git diff --check (clean). Additionally exported a trimmed copy of the real project-workflows-001 run (original untouched): version 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0, definition unchanged, lane evidence preserved, and the server adapter projects the before and after exports identically. Live smoke (section 8) and browser suites not run.
open_assumptions: Deviation from PRD section 3: `both` is added to the reserved lane ids (schemas, controller, server) so the legacy attribution cannot collide with a configured lane; the PRD list did not include it.
reviewCompletion.schema.json accepts files spelling version 1.0.0 or 1.1.0 under the same 1.1.0 rules; the reviewer prompt example now writes 1.1.0.

Runs prepared before this slice that are still mid-flight cannot resume with the new graph (their checkpoints use ui/adapter/ui_packet keys); finished runs re-export at 1.3.0 with that evidence carried under values.lanes/values.packets. All known existing runs are finished.
PRD open questions resolved by their defaults: prepare accepts --workers too; panes never wrap; the manual freeze CLI requires --handoff for every selected lane.

zod cannot import verification.schema.json (if/then/else), so the TypeScript contract test checks that schema structurally and the pattern directly; policies are validated against it by the Python tests (test_verification, test_lanes). feature.schema.json and reviewCompletion.schema.json are imported and exercised with zod. The reserved-id rule is spelled as a lookahead in the pattern, not a `not` keyword, for the same reason.

The server treats a finding whose worker is neither a lane of the run nor multiple/none/both as RUN_STORAGE_INVALID, and pre-1.3.0 exports derive required_check_kinds from the role (frontend: build, browser; backend: unit) because their controller enforced exactly that.
LangGraph max_concurrency is max(2, number of selected lanes) so every lane's fan-out step may run concurrently.

features/worker-lanes/feature.json (this run's own feature, outside adapter ownership) stays at 1.0.0 and now launches through the translation path with a deprecation line; the UI worker builds against contracts/projects 1.3.0 as described in the PRD without deviation beyond the reserved `both`.
